title: The Pulse, Monday 30 September 2026
tldr: OpenAI's DevDay brought GPT-6.1 Sol (near-Astra performance at 1/5th the cost, purpose-built for coding agents), always-on Dots assistants, and Codex cloud environments. The big shift: agents can now close the laptop and keep working — exactly the direction our Botterfly and EverRaise workflows need.

models.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.summary: OpenAI's new model delivers near-Astra intelligence for coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra's API prices, with 95% cached input discount.
models.why: Directly relevant to our wehshi PR review panels and Botterfly coding tasks — we can run stronger agents without blowing the budget, and reuse PR context across multiple review rounds.

research.title: Divide and Inject: Can Agents Reconstruct an Indirect Prompt Injection from Fragments?
research.summary: Agentic systems that orchestrate tools and reason over long contexts face a new attack surface: indirect prompt injection spread across retrieved document fragments.
research.why: Our RAG systems for Mackinac and EverRaise retrieve untrusted content — this shows attackers don't need a complete malicious instruction in one place.

research.title: τ-Multilingual: Benchmarking Voice Agents Across Languages
research.summary: Extends τ-Voice benchmark to Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Korean, and Mandarin with native-speaker evaluation of full-duplex voice agent calls.
research.why: EverRaise voice agents on Vapi speak English only right now — if we expand to Spanish-speaking campaigns this benchmark is the eval we'd run.

research.title: FD-VAD: Semantic Endpoint Detection for Streaming Full-Duplex Speech
research.summary: Determines from partial speech whether a pause reflects hesitation or completed intent, without cascading through ASR.
research.why: EverRaise voice campaigns need natural turn-taking — this gives us a semantic detector to avoid cutting callers off mid-thought.

research.title: Lost in Conversation or Lost in Translation? Diagnosing Multi-Turn Degradation in RAG
research.summary: Multi-turn RAG conversations degrade as follow-up questions build toward multi-hop queries; paper proposes diagnostics to separate retrieval from reasoning failures.
research.why: Mackinac's legislative research involves long multi-turn back-and-forth — if recall collapses after turn three we need to see whether it's retrieval or reasoning.

research.title: Auditable Long-Term Memory: A Deterministic Retrieval Chain Measured at 479/475 of 500 on LongMemEval-S
research.summary: Hybrid candidate retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, coverage-first compilation, and deterministic scaffolds; LLM used only as a replaceable final reader.
research.why: Our Hermes Mnemosyne memory system uses a similar chain — this validates the architecture and shows reranking before packing context is table stakes.

releases.title: LangChain Anthropic 1.7.5
releases.summary: Adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 compatibility and fixes invalid tool call serialization on replay.
releases.why: We use LangChain for some Pipeline client flows — the Sonnet 5.5 compat means we can test it without waiting for upstream fixes.

releases.title: Langfuse 4.47.0
releases.summary: Native JS events through NAPI, ClickHouse write strategy, AI gateway trace environment control, and transcript turn nesting exposure.
releases.why: We use Langfuse to trace EverRaise and SalesKick production calls — the ClickHouse write path and transcript turn introspection both land in our observability stack.

releases.title: Next.js 16.3.7
releases.summary: Backports a turbo-tasks-backend fix for strongly consistent read hanging on canceled tasks.
releases.why: Chrysalis and the Pipeline client dashboards run Next.js — canceled task hangs in turbo-tasks mean broken deploys.

hackernews.title: Dots: Always-on agents
hackernews.summary: OpenAI's always-on assistants with their own cloud computers that keep working after you close the laptop, powered by GPT-6 Astra.
hackernews.why: Close fit to what Botterfly is becoming — we want the agent to triage PRs, file issues, and run long tasks without babysitting.

hackernews.title: A Privacy Analysis of Web and Mobile Conversational AI Agents [pdf]
hackernews.summary: Academic study of privacy leakage in conversational AI agents across web and mobile, with 412 points and engineering-focused discussion.
hackernews.why: EverRaise voice agents and Botterfly integrations both handle user data — this flags what trackers and third parties see in production conversation flows.

hackernews.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
hackernews.summary: Anthropic research on how GLM-5.3's release lowers the barrier to advanced cyber capabilities and what that means for model deployment policy.
hackernews.why: We use Claude across SalesKick and Pipeline work — understanding Anthropic's threat model helps us reason about what guardrails to expect in future releases.

hackernews.title: Livenerf: Has Opus 5.5 been nerfed yet?
hackernews.summary: Community-run tracker that monitors whether Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 behavior has changed since release, with 364 points overnight.
hackernews.why: We pin wehshi to Opus — if Anthropic silently nerfs the model, this tracker catches it before we spend a sprint debugging phantom regressions.

x_posts.title: Codex cloud environments (OpenAI Developers)
x_posts.summary: OpenAI launched persistent Codex cloud environments: reusable setups with repo, dependencies, scripts, and settings already in place so agents keep working when you close the laptop.
x_posts.why: Exactly what we want for Botterfly long-running reviews and DSPy optimization loops — no more keeping a session open to babysit the agent.

x_posts.title: Nous Research partners with OpenAI for ChatGPT sign-in
x_posts.summary: Nous Research integrated ChatGPT sign-in for the Nous Portal, letting users apply their ChatGPT plan to Hermes Agent with visibility in ChatGPT settings.
x_posts.why: We run Botterfly on Hermes Agent — this means our team can use their existing ChatGPT plans instead of managing separate billing.

closing: Models: Only one new model family in the window (GPT-6.1 Sol), but it's the one that matters.
